TACC PHONE HELP

Note Your Last Official Duty

  • Offloads can take much longer
  • Min cut is 17 from LDG to TO
  • 12 for LFA (from last duty, usually +45)

TACC Shift Change

  • Day Shift — 1200z–2000z
  • Swing Shift — 2000z–0400z
  • Mid Shift — 0400z–1200z

Overfly

Call bases involved.

  • Saves time on a late trip
  • Gets the airplane home early
  • Bad base for support, cold etc.

Duty Day Leg Requirements

  • Basic Day — less than below
  • Basic Aug Day — 1x5hr or 2x3hrs
  • Augmented Day — 1x6hr or 2x4hrs
  • Can swap upload for 1 leg ^

Flight Duty Periods

  • Basic 16hrs
  • Basic Aug — 18hr
  • Augmented 24hr

To Justify a CECR 3 hr max w/o the senior

  • Hot meals. Look up times of restaurants, Shoppette etc. Limited amount of actual food.
  • Quiet hours 202v3 reg, should approve CECR de-positioning legs.
  • Home for the RDAP (4 am Travis time, not midnight)
  • Bottom of circadian rhythm — use their G2 products against them.
  • We took mins this whole trip? Our guys are exhausted.
  • We called for cargo, they won't have any for us — we don't need the extra time for an upload.
  • I'm on a checkride, please sir.
  • There's about to be a crew mutiny.
  • We have XXX hours of slop in our schedule for quiet hours tomorrow.

How SELCAL Works

The Code

Every tail is assigned a unique 4-letter SELCAL code, built from 16 possible letters — A through S, skipping I, N, and O (they're too easy to confuse with 1, 4, and 0). That gives 65,780 possible 4-letter combinations, more than enough for every airframe in the fleet.

The Tones

Each letter maps to one specific audio tone. The 16 tones aren't spaced randomly — they climb geometrically from 312.6 Hz up to 1479.1 Hz, each one about 10.9% higher than the last:

fn = fA × r(n−1)    r ≈ 1.109

That even spacing keeps every tone easy to tell apart from its neighbors, while keeping the whole set inside the same voiceband your HF/VHF radio already carries.

The Transmission

SELCAL never sends all 4 letters at once. It sends two dual-tone pulses back to back — each pulse is two frequencies playing together, which is just their waveforms added:

s(t) = sin(2πf1t) + sin(2πf2t)

Pulse 1 carries letters 1–2 for about 1.0 second, then a ~0.2 second gap, then pulse 2 carries letters 3–4 for another 1.0 second. That's exactly what happens when you hit "Test SELCAL Tone" above.

The Decode

Your aircraft's SELCAL decoder is always listening, filtering the incoming audio through narrow bandpass filters tuned to those 16 tones. It only chimes when it sees its own two exact tone-pairs, in the right order, held for the right duration — everyone else's calls pass through silently.

MARS RADIO HOW-TO

MILITARY AUXILIARY RADIO SYSTEM — HF PHONE PATCH PROCEDURE
Courtesy and brevity keep the frequency open for the next aircraft in need of a patch.
INFO SECTION

WHAT IS MARS? (Click for more)

WHAT IS MARS?

The Military Auxiliary Radio System is a DoD-sponsored program of licensed volunteer operators who provide auxiliary and emergency HF communications support.

SERVICES PROVIDED

  • DSN & commercial phone patches
  • Radio checks and propagation reports
  • SELCAL confirmation, METAR / TAF relay

THE OPERATORS

These are the unsung heroes of the HF bands: deeply feral radio nerds lurking in lightless, unventilated basements.

Behind the Mic: Sustained entirely by scalding Hot Pockets, pure spite, and severe vitamin D deficiency, these subterranean goblins spend 18 hours a day arguing on Reddit about antenna impedance while wallowing in their own filth. Their underground fortresses feature crusty, biohazard-grade “NO GIRLS ALLOWED” signs taped over the door to guard glowing vacuum tubes and greasy coaxial cables. They don’t shower, touch grass, or wear real pants. They just sit in the damp dark surrounded by overflowing trash, absorbing furnace fumes, and screaming into the electromagnetic void.

The “War Hero” Complex: Because this program is a direct holdover from WWII, passing a single routine radio check for a Reach plane instantly turns them into a battle-hardened savior in their own mind. They’ll immediately post a 3,000-word essay to r/hamradio detailing how they personally saved an airborne asset from “total disaster,” reaping hundreds of upvotes from equally unwashed neckbeards.

The Subterranean Lifeline: Yet, when you’re mid-ocean with zero satellite coverage, a feral hermit who hasn’t seen sunlight or a woman since 2017 is unironically your only link back to human civilization—standing a 24/7 watch simply because they have nowhere else to go.

1SELECT THE FREQUENCYALWAYS USB
Primary13927.0 kHz USB
Alternate 111407.0 kHz USB
Alternate 27633.5 kHz USB
Tertiary4557.0 kHz USB
“START HIGH, WORK LOW”
2MAKE THE CALL
"MARSRADIO, THIS IS RCH69420, NORTH ATLANTIC, OVER."

State your callsign and general position. Keep the initial call short and clear.

REPEAT AS NEEDED — THEY ARE ALWAYS LISTENING
3ANTENNA ALIGNMENT

Give your general position and heading in your initial call — this lets the station's directional beam antenna be aimed toward you for the strongest signal.

Weak or broken copy is often solved simply by the operator re-pointing their array once they know roughly where you are.

4THANK THE OPERATOR

MARS operators are unpaid volunteers who maintain their own equipment and stand watch on their own time.

A clear "thank you, MARS, out" at the end of the patch goes a long way — and is always appreciated.
